title: Prompt Editor
summary: Open Settings → Agent behavior → Prompts → Open Prompt Editor, or choose Prompt Editor in Directory. Direct links use /prompt-editor?key=prompt.identifier.
html:
Prompt Editor

Open Settings → Agent behavior → Prompts → Open Prompt Editor, or choose Prompt Editor in Directory. Direct links use /prompt-editor?key=prompt.identifier.

The editor includes system instructions, runtime guidance, skill and tool wording, recovery instructions, and helper templates. Search names, identifiers, or text; filter by group, skill, customized entries, or changed defaults. Each entry shows its usage source and required variables.

Edit the full or compact wording and select Save, or press Ctrl/Cmd+S. The selected wording indicator follows the existing Compact guidance settings. Where no separate compact wording exists, both modes use the full prompt. Saving an inactive variant does not switch the guidance setting.

Turning Compact guidance off selects full wording, including your full override if one is saved. Use Restore variant to return that wording to the shipped default. Disabling compact mode alone does not remove custom instructions.

Default comparison displays the shipped text beside your draft. Rendered preview substitutes sample values you supply without calling a model. Template variables are required; unknown variables, malformed placeholders, and empty instructions are rejected. Literal dollar signs in templates use $$.

Changes apply installation-wide at the next model request, including requests within active tasks. Requests already in flight and their retries keep their original instructions. The editor reports when active changes have reached disk. If another editor saved first, a conflict preserves your draft; copy it before reloading the current prompt.

Saving first makes the change active; the disk-status message tracks its recovery checkpoint separately. If it reports that saving needs attention, inspect persistence in Settings before treating the change as safely stored for restart.

Restore variant removes that wording's override. Restore this prompt removes both variants. Restore all prompts removes every override, including retired entries. Reset confirmations show the affected count. These actions leave Compact guidance selection settings unchanged.

Application releases provide a read-only prompts.db. Your customizations live in userprompts.db through the Controller's existing checkpoint and recovery system. An update preserves your wording and flags changes to its underlying default. An incompatible imported template remains inspectable while the runtime uses its shipped default. Retired prompts remain inspectable but are not used automatically. Backups include overrides; clearing execution history preserves them.

The editor changes authored instructions. Tool schemas, permission enforcement, user messages, retrieved documents, and runtime values remain independently owned.
